subject: Edge vendor renewal — split-bid strategy & checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@cloudflare.com>, Tom Simmons <tom.simmons@fastly.com>, Jen Morales <legal@akamai.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Edge vendor renewal — split-bid strategy & checklist

Team —

Our existing contracts with Cloudflare and Fastly expire Q1 2027 (Akamai is on a rolling contract but we should consolidate the RFP). Before we commit to a one-vendor renewal, procurement asked us to evaluate a split-bid approach to preserve leverage and resilience. Id like to kick off a short cross-functional pulse to:

- Confirm requirements (security evidence, egress/cdn pricing, WAF rulesets, bot management)
- Get updated SOW/pricing from each vendor for a like-for-like set of routes
- Decide on a 60-day pilot window for technical validation if both vendors can meet latency/SLOs

Attached: CF_SOW_v1 (vendor-draft) and our historical usage extract. Please review and add any missing checklist items. Laura: can procurement prepare an RFP template we can use to collect apples-to-apples pricing?

Next steps I propose:
1) Vendors send revised SOW + itemized pricing by EOD Thu 11/26
2) Security team to confirm required evidence (SOC 2, penetration test reports, contractual data residency language) by Mon 11/29
3) Engineering to propose a limited pilot route list (3-5 high-traffic routes) by Wed 12/01

Ill own coordinating the pilot and tracking latency/cost delta. Looping legal early (Jen) for any amendment templates.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Product, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Park <sara@cloudflare.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Simmons <tom.simmons@fastly.com>, Jen Morales <legal@akamai.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge vendor renewal — split-bid strategy & checklist

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the note and for looping us in. I've attached an updated SOW (CF_SOW_v2.pdf) that aligns to the 3-route pilot and calls out WAF managed rules, bot management tiers, and egress pricing tiers. A few quick pieces:

- We can offer a multi-year discount if you commit to a 24-month term; I put a placeholder line item but understand you want to compare options.
- SOC 2 Type II and latest pen-test summary are available — Ive included a link to our security pack in the attachment list.
- Were open to a 60-day pilot; we recommend synthetic traffic tests + a parallel run to validate cache hit patterns.

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute readout next week to walk through the SOW and where we've built configurability for Redwoods use cases.

Best,
Sara Park
Enterprise Sales, Cloudflare
Attachments: CF_SOW_v2.pdf; CF_security_pack_link.txt

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge vendor renewal — split-bid strategy & checklist

Karthik / all —

Agree with the split-bid approach for now. Procurement will issue a condensed RFP (attached template) that enforces:

- Standardized service matrix (WAF rules, bot management, DDoS mitigation, CDN cache tiers)
- Clear egress / request pricing and an example monthly bill for 3 payload profiles
- Security artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, latest pentest summary, fourth-party risk attestation
- Contractual SLAs (p99 latency targets, error-rate SLOs), and remediation / credits language
- Data residency & log retention controls (KMS/HSM references where applicable)

Action items for vendors: please submit the RFP with itemized pricing and any proposed amendments to standard T&Cs by Thu 11/26 EOD — if you need a short extension let me know. Well run a legal redline pass after we receive submissions.

Timeline: Procurement issues RFP to all three vendors today and will collect responses in the Drive folder (link below). Post-collection well schedule a commercial review (vendors only) and a technical deep-dive with engineering.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/edge-renewal-2026

Laura Bennett
Sr. Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Sara Park <sara@cloudflare.com>, Tom Simmons <tom.simmons@fastly.com>, Jen Morales <legal@akamai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge vendor renewal — split-bid strategy & checklist

Team / vendors —

Quick update from engineering after a spike test last week: both Cloudflare and Fastly meet our baseline p99 latency on the pilot routes, but cache-hit behavior is materially different for API payloads (CF tends to have a higher sustained hit rate on the JSON endpoints). Given that, I recommend the following path forward:

1) Run a 45-day parallel pilot (Cloudflare + Fastly) on the agreed route list. Well route 30% traffic split and collect latency/cost/hit-rate metrics.
2) Legal to prepare a one-page amendment template for each vendor that contains: pilot duration, SLA measurement method, data handling commitments, and pilot termination terms (Jen).
3) Procurement to collect final itemized pricing and confirm any negotiated term discounts — Laura, please confirm whether were comfortable with staggered renewals if one vendor offers better economics.

Attachments: Fastly_pricing_sheet_v1.xlsx, Akamai_security_evidence.zip

Ill stand up a short dashboards board (Latency / Cost / HitRate) and share a readout at the pilot midpoint. If vendors can supply DocuSign-ready amendments it will speed time-to-pilot.

Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Edge Services
